title: Emma Raducanu withdraws from Wimbledon with stress fracture
snippet: # Emma Raducanu withdraws from Wimbledon with stress fracture. British No 1 says it is ‘difficult to process’ that injury is preventing her from competing at this year’s Championships. Emma Raducanu practised earlier on Sunday but has since been forced to withdraw through injury   Credit: Shaun Broo

Published 28 June 2026 10:09pm BST Emma Raducanu has announced her withdrawal from Wimbledon at the 11th hour after developing a stress fracture in her right shin.The news came late on Sunday evening, after the 23-year-old had previously indicated her intention to play through the pain against Antonia Ruzic on Monday afternoon.“I can’t believe I’m saying this,” Raducanu wrote in a post on Instagram, “but sadly I’ve had to withdraw from this year’s Wimbledon.“I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.“Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process.“I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.” Raducanu trained with strapping on her right shin on Sunday morning Credit: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images During her press conference earlier on Sunday, Raducanu said she had developed the beginnings of this problem during “the back-end of the clay-court season”.Even at the time, some expert observers had questioned the scheduling that saw Raducanu rush back on the clay after a lengthy absence from the tour. From there, she went on to play five matches in a week at Queen’s Club, including three in the space of 28 hours as rain delays wreaked havoc on the schedule.Raducanu is sometimes accused of hypochondria, given the number of tournaments she has missed on account of injury, but this latest bulletin reveals that she is also capable of pushing through significant pain.Having skipped training for four days between Tuesday and Friday to rest the problem area, she then spent the best part of three hours on the practice court over the weekend in a last-ditch attempt to prove her fitness for Wimbledon. Raducanu said missing out on Wimbledon was ‘hard to process’ Credit: Andrew Matthews/PA Earlier in the day, she had told reporters that she was prepared to risk further damage to her body because of the importance of this event. “There are certain tournaments you’re willing to do more for, put yourself on the line more for, risk more for,” Raducanu explained. “For me, of course, Wimbledon is that.“I don’t think any doctor can tell me I’m not going to make it worse. I just have to be aware of the risks I’m taking stepping out on to the court, weighing up if I’m willing to do that.”Even though Raducanu has suffered a variety of niggling injuries and illnesses over the past three years, a stress fracture represents her most serious setback since the surgery she had on both wrists and one ankle in May 2023.The recovery time is estimated as somewhere between six and 12 weeks, which means that she looks unlikely to recover in time for the US Open – or the Billie Jean King Cup finals in Shenzhen that follow swiftly thereafter.With only 21 matches under her belt this se
